$ git log --oneline issue..fix

🧬 Anatomy of a Fix

What 129 real bug reports, their fixes and their tests teach a Gemma 4 agent
● the issue ● the fix ● the test ● the agent
Every task in this competition is a three-part story. Someone **reports** a problem, someone **fixes** it, someone **tests** it. The hidden grader keeps only the last part: your agent reads the report, writes the fix, and the test decides whether it counts. There is no partial credit. This notebook follows the three parts through the 129 public development tasks. At the end it builds a Gemma 4 agent whose rules come from what the data shows. Each chapter ends with a **→ for the agent** line. | Chapter | Question | |:--|:--| | **I. The issue** | What does the agent actually get to read? | | **II. The fix** | How big is a correct answer, and where does it live? | | **III. The test** | What decides pass or fail? | | **IV. The gap** | How far is the issue text from the fix site? | | **V. A case file** | One task, end to end | | **VI.
